_comment: Clayworks LITE — settings.example.json. NOT a drop-in replacement for ~/.claude/settings.json. I pick the blocks I want and merge them into my existing settings.json. I know the _comment fields are not part of any CC schema; Claude Code tolerates them, but I strip them once I'm done customizing.
_comment_general: Three example hook blocks are shown below. Each maps to a LITE artifact: UserPromptSubmit feeds the Nudge skill, SessionStart and Stop are the starting points for the heartbeat-concept pattern. See hooks/examples/ for the full per-event contracts.
_comment_install_path: I use the UserPromptSubmit Nudge block for the install.sh / install.ps1 path only. If you installed LITE as a plugin (/plugin install clayworks-lite@clayworks-lite), I already register that hook through the plugin; if I added it here too, I'd see every due alert twice.
_comment_chaining: I rely on Claude Code running all hooks that match an event in parallel, not in the order listed, so I never make one hook depend on another's output. If I already have hooks for an event, I append new entries to its 'hooks' array rather than replace the array. I know hook entries from user, project, and local settings merge rather than override each other. To chain a second UserPromptSubmit hook (e.g. a freshness gate that injects current docs when CC features come up), I add another {"type": "command", ...} object next to the Nudge entry; I show the contract in hooks/examples/userpromptsubmit.sh.

hooks._comment: Nudge skill consumer (script install only) — I surface due alerts to Claude on each prompt. I have run-python.sh find python3, python, or py -3 and exit silently if none exists. I cover the details in skills/clayworks-lite-nudge/SKILL.md.

Optional. I copy hooks/examples/sessionstart.sh to ~/.claude/hooks/sessionstart.sh FIRST, then customize; until the file exists, I'd see a hook error from this entry at every session start. In the starter example I surface a primer file at ~/agent/session-primer.md and warn about uncommitted git state in cwd, branching on the payload's 'source' field.

Optional. I run it after every Claude response (not at session exit). I copy hooks/examples/stop.sh to ~/.claude/hooks/stop.sh FIRST, then customize. In the starter example I log turn ends and show the gated 24h-trigger pattern for background work (e.g. dream-style memory consolidation). I describe the broader cadence pattern in the heartbeat-concept skill.

_comment_permissions: I add a top-level 'permissions' block to allowlist common commands and reduce permission prompts. I follow https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings for the schema. I use Claude Code's bundled /fewer-permission-prompts skill to scan recent transcripts and suggest a starter allowlist.
_comment_env: I add a top-level 'env' block for environment variables I want set when CC runs (project-relevant paths, debug flags, etc.). Strict JSON — string values only. I keep secrets out of this file and load them from my shell's secret store instead.
_comment_plugins: If you install LITE-recommended plugins (Engram for memory, Honcho for user modeling), they manage their own settings.json entries when added via /plugin install. See the LITE README's Acknowledgments for the upstream repos and skills/clayworks-lite-memory-routing/SKILL.md for the marketplace-add commands.
